record.paper_title: The Strong Convergence of Subgradients of Convex Functions Along Directions: Perspectives and Open Problems
record.original_question: For which nonzero directions w does the directional subdifferential limit lim_{t↓0} ∂f(x + t w) exist as a singleton rather than as a larger set? The paper singles this out as a particularly demanding version of the directional convergence problem.

evidence.quote: we should also add the following question: for which directions is the limit, in (3), a singleton? Perhaps this question is the most demanding and will require a lot of work to be elaborated properly.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a Banach space with topological dual $X^*$, and let $f:X\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}$ be a proper, lower semicontinuous convex function. For a point $x\in\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom} f)$, the (Fenchel–Moreau) subdifferential is
$$\partial f(x)=\{x^*\in X^*:\ f(y)\geq f(x)+\langle x^*,y-x\rangle\ \text{for all }y\in X\}.$$
For a nonzero direction $w\in X\setminus\{0\}$ and $t>0$ small enough that $x+tw\in\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom} f)$, consider the set-valued limit superior (in the norm topology of $X^*$)
$$L(x,w)\;:=\;\limsup_{t\downarrow 0}\partial f(x+tw)\;=\;\bigl\{x^*\in X^*:\ \exists\,t_n\downarrow 0,\ \exists\,x_n^*\in\partial f(x+t_nw)\ \text{with}\ \|x_n^*-x^*\|\to 0\bigr\}.$$

Characterize, in terms of $f$, $x$, and the geometry of $X$, those nonzero directions $w$ for which the limit $\lim_{t\downarrow 0}\partial f(x+tw)$ exists and equals a singleton $\{x^*\}\subset X^*$ in the norm topology (rather than merely a larger set of cluster points). Equivalently, determine necessary and sufficient conditions on $w$ ensuring that $L(x,w)$ reduces to a single element and that every selection $t\mapsto x_t^*\in\partial f(x+tw)$ converges in norm to that element as $t\downarrow 0$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open question in the literature on directional convergence of subgradients of convex functions on Banach spaces. No subsequent paper appears to have given a general characterization; the question is described as the most demanding version of the directional convergence problem, and recent surveys still list it among the open problems in this area.

status_evidence.title: The Strong Convergence of Subgradients of Convex Functions Along Directions: Perspectives and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Perspectives and open problems concerning strong convergence of subgradients along directions in convex analysis.
status_evidence.claim: The singleton-limit version of the directional subdifferential convergence problem is stated as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: On the Strong Convergence of Subgradients of Convex Functions
status_evidence.snippet: Investigates relative compactness in norm of subdifferentials along a direction; in infinite dimensions even existence of limits is delicate.
status_evidence.claim: Even existence of norm limits of subgradients along a direction is generally not known in infinite-dimensional Banach spaces, supporting that the singleton-limit characterization remains open.
